stem.en: On the Atlantic Ocean floor, rock is youngest at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and older further away on both sides. Why?

text.en: Plates move apart and magma fills the gap

feedback.en: Yes. New crust forms at the ridge, and older crust moves away.

text.en: Plates push together and pile old rock up

feedback.en: No. The ridge is a boundary where plates move apart.

text.en: Plates slide past and drag young rock along

feedback.en: No. Sliding plates make no new crust.

text.en: Old rock sinks and leaves the young rock on top

feedback.en: No. The young rock is at the ridge, and old rock lies to the sides.

explanation.en: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a divergent boundary. As the plates move apart, magma rises and forms new crust at the ridge. Older crust is carried away on both sides.

hints.en: Which way do the plates move at a mid-ocean ridge?
